acceptanceCovered: Route /kudos/new is auth-guarded: an unauthenticated visitor is redirected to /login, while an authenticated one gets the form -- verified in proxy.ts (isGuarded checks pathname === "/kudos/new" || startsWith("/kudos/new/")) and e2e/route-guard.spec.ts ID-1; part of the 62-pass compose gate.

The public Kudos read surface stays public: /kudos, /kudos/[id] and /kudos/secret-box are unaffected by the new guard -- verified proxy.ts uses exact-path match, never a bare startsWith("/kudos"); K-21/kudos-live-board*.spec.ts remain in the 144-pass full run.

The modal renders the h1 'Gui loi cam on va ghi nhan den dong doi' and the fields in the frame's order: recipient, title, body editor, hashtags, images, anonymous checkbox, footer actions -- verified compose-form.tsx renders h1 then FieldRow(recipient) -> FieldRow(title) -> body editor -> hashtag FieldRow -> image FieldRow -> AnonymousToggle -> ComposeActions in that literal source order.

Recipient autocomplete filters by query, trims whitespace, shows an empty state, and selecting an option fills the field and closes the menu -- verified recipient-picker.tsx: trimmedQuery, foldVietnameseText diacritic-insensitive filter, recipient-empty testid, onSelect fills field and clears query state.

The Danh hieu title field renders its placeholder and both helper lines and is required -- verified title-field.tsx wiring to copy.placeholders.title/hints.titleLine1/titleLine2, and validateCompose() flags title required.

The rich-text toolbar offers bold, italic, strikethrough, ordered list, link and quote, with the link button opening a URL dialog -- verified rich-text-toolbar.tsx six buttons + link-dialog.tsx URL input/confirm wired to toggleInlineMark/toggleBlockMark in rich-text.ts.

Typing @ opens a mention menu that narrows as the name continues and inserts the chosen colleague, matching names without diacritics -- verified use-body-editor-controller.ts foldVietnameseText (NFD normalize + explicit d/D fold) reused identically by recipient-picker.tsx and mention-menu.tsx, and insertMention() in rich-text.ts stores the sunnerId run.

Hashtags are chips: at least 1 required, at most 5, a sixth is refused with 'Toi da 5 hashtag' while the add button stays visible, and removing one chip leaves the others -- verified hashtag-picker.tsx (hashtag-add stays rendered, hashtag-error on tooMany) and validateCompose()/create_kudos SQL both enforcing 1-5.

Images: a jpg and a png attach and show a thumbnail of that file, a pdf is rejected with a format error, the add button is hidden at 5 and returns after a removal -- verified image-picker.tsx (image-add hidden at MAX_IMAGES, image-error on rejection) and isAcceptedImageType()/upload-kudos-image.ts server-side MIME re-check.

The anonymous checkbox is unchecked by default and checking it reveals an anonymous name input that hides again when unchecked -- verified anonymous-toggle.tsx checked=false initial state and conditional render of anonymous-name-input.

Submitting an empty form shows all four required-field errors simultaneously with 'Khong duoc de trong' and does not submit -- verified validateCompose() never early-returns and sets all of recipient/title/body/hashtag at once; compose-form.tsx's handleSubmit dispatches setErrors and returns before calling submit() when any error exists.

The submit button is never disabled and instead carries data-submit-ready reflecting whether the required fields are filled -- verified compose-actions.tsx never sets disabled/aria-disabled on compose-submit and isSubmitReady()/data-submit-ready reflects state, matching the ratified test-contract.md amendment.
Cancel navigates to /kudos and saves nothing -- verified compose-actions.tsx compose-cancel links to CANCEL_HREF = "/kudos" with no dispatch/submit call.

A successful submit lands on /kudos with the new Kudos visible on the board, proving the row reached Postgres -- verified create-kudos.ts calls supabase.rpc("create_kudos") then redirect("/kudos") only on success; live psql run of create_kudos produced a real row (id 65-67 in the adversarial session) and the seeded+e2e-created row count is 62 in the live database.

Every rule is re-validated server-side in the action, so a client that bypasses the UI is still rejected -- verified create-kudos.ts calls validateCompose(payload) independently of the client, and create_kudos SQL re-checks receiver existence, campaign/message non-blank, message_format, and hashtag count 1-5 regardless of caller.

RLS makes a forged sender impossible: sender_id must resolve through sunners.auth_user_id to the session, and anon cannot insert at all -- verified LIVE by adversarial psql: anon direct INSERT into kudos raised 'new row violates row-level security policy'; an authenticated JWT for an unrelated uid attempting sender_id=1 also raised the same RLS violation; anon calling the create_kudos RPC raised 'create_kudos requires an authenticated session'; live pg_policies confirms kudos_insert_own's with_check joins sunners.auth_user_id = auth.uid() and no UPDATE/DELETE policy exists on kudos, kudos_hashtags, kudos_attachments or sunners.

A signed-in user with no sunners row is auto-provisioned exactly once, idempotently under double submit -- verified LIVE by inserting a throwaway auth.users row and calling create_kudos twice in the same session: exactly one sunners row was created (on conflict (auth_user_id) do nothing), full_name/avatar_url/department_id resolved to the documented fallbacks (Unassigned department, sample-avatar.png).

The Kudos Live Board renders 'doc' messages as safe React elements and anonymous senders via a dedicated chip, with malformed documents degrading to plain text -- verified kudos-message-body.tsx never uses dangerouslySetInnerHTML, walks parseKudosDoc's output into <span>/<a>/<strong> elements, degrades to the raw message string when parseKudosDoc returns null, and re-checks the link scheme allow-list at render time independent of the parser; parseKudosDoc in rich-text.ts rejects malformed JSON, unknown block/run types, and non-allow-listed link schemes by returning null.

F004 does not regress: all 57 seeded rows stay plain and non-anonymous and the shipped board suite stays green -- verified LIVE via psql: all 57 seeded kudos rows have message_format='plain' and is_anonymous=false; kudos-card.tsx's diff is purely additive (conditional AnonymousSenderChip swap-in, KudosMessageBody wraps the identical

markup); temper-results.json records the 144-pass full run twice consecutively with kudos_likes back to 0.

New INSERT policies as the precedent for future write tables -- read the migration and live pg_policies output: all four INSERT policies bridge through sunners.auth_user_id = (select auth.uid()) or auth_user_id = (select auth.uid()) directly, matching the kudos_likes_insert_own idiom already shipped; confirmed no UPDATE/DELETE policy exists on any of the four tables.

findings.summary: compose-form.tsx and lib/kudos/board-data.ts land at exactly 200 lines, not strictly under the repo's 200-line file-size guideline (development-rules.md). Not a lint/build failure and not a maintainability problem in practice, but literally at rather than under the stated cap.

validateCompose() checks hashtag count (>MAX_HASHTAGS) but never checks imageUrls.length > MAX_IMAGES; the >5-images rule is enforced only inside the create_kudos SQL function, one layer further out than the hashtag path's two-layer defense. Functionally safe -- a bypass still gets rejected by the database -- but it surfaces as a generic {form:"unknown"} error rather than a field-specific one, and is inconsistent with the stated 'every rule is re-checked server-side in the action' framing.

isAcceptedImageType(file.type) trusts the client-declared File.type rather than sniffing file content/magic bytes, so an attacker can label arbitrary bytes as image/jpeg and have them stored and publicly served from the kudos-attachments bucket under that content-type. Low risk here (not renderable as HTML/JS since it's served with an image content-type, and next/image only ever consumes it as an source) but worth hardening if the bucket's threat model grows.
